question.text: Antyodaya Seva Sangh's rural development impact trend dipped 18% in FY 2024-25 due to drought in the intervention block. As per Chapter 7.3.2, what is the SIA's correct reporting stance?

answer.text: Report the dip and explicitly disclose the external cause (natural calamity) as a reason for underachievement
Smooth the dip using a three-year rolling average and suppress the one-year drop
Exclude the drought-affected block from the reporting boundary
Restate prior-year numbers downward to normalise the trend

explanation.text: The Logic: Chapter 7.3.2 states: 'Reasons/ causes for underachievement also need to be reported' and distinguishes internal vs external (regulatory, natural or manmade calamity, socio-political) causes. Smoothing, excluding or restating violates transparency and materiality principles. The Trap: A is a manipulation that a weak SIA might agree to; a regulator will flag it. C is boundary manipulation. D is prior-period restatement which is not permitted for impact disclosures without a formal error correction footnote. Cross-Exam Context: Similar to 'material adverse change' reporting in LODR Reg 30 (III-A/III-C Compliance) — bad news must be disclosed, not suppressed. Assessor's Pro-Tip: When disclosing a dip, structure the paragraph as: (i) quantified dip, (ii) root cause (internal/external), (iii) management response, (iv) revised next-year target. This mirrors the MD&A discipline and satisfies both SIR readers and SEBI inspectors.
